bullets.title: Three reasons growth slowed in H1
bullets.lead: Each one is fixable within the next two quarters.

items.heading: Fewer new customers
items.body: Paid acquisition cost rose 28%, so we cut spend and new-customer volume fell.

items.heading: Lower basket size online
items.body: Free-shipping threshold pushed small baskets to competitors.

items.heading: Store openings slipped
items.body: Five of eight planned openings moved to H2 because of permits.

faq.title: Questions we expect from the board

items.heading: What if the forecasting pilot underperforms?
items.body: The pilot has a three-month gate; below 85% accuracy we keep manual approval, so store operations are not affected.

items.heading: Will remodels hurt sales during the works?
items.body: Stores stay open and remodel in phases. Each store is affected for about two weeks, under 0.3% of annual revenue.

items.heading: What is the main risk of the Balanced option?
items.body: Site selection and group-buying competition. We hold a 15% budget buffer to adjust the store plan mid-year.

converge.title: Three signals point to the same priority
converge.lead: Membership and supply chain are our most certain levers.

points.heading: Demand
points.body: Member frequency and basket size keep rising

points.heading: Cost
points.body: Spoilage and fulfilment still have room to fall

points.heading: Competition
points.body: Peers lag clearly on supply chain capability

converge.conclusion: Put 70% of incremental FY2027 investment into members and supply chain.

drivers.title: Three gaps hold back profit flexibility

points.heading: High fresh spoilage
points.body: Every 1 pt of spoilage costs about $17M in profit

points.heading: Rising acquisition cost
points.body: Online new-customer cost is up 28% year over year

points.heading: Uneven store productivity
points.body: Bottom 20% of stores sell a third of the top tier

drivers.conclusion: The bottleneck is supply chain and store mix, not demand.

pyramid.title: One goal, three supporting moves
pyramid.conclusion: Grow revenue 15%, lift net margin to 4.5% and reach 2.6M paid members.

points.heading: Deepen membership

points.heading: Automate supply
points.body: Roll out forecasting to every store and fresh category

points.heading: Reshape the network

matrix.title: Start with two quick wins, fund two strategic bets

quadrants.heading: Quick wins
quadrants.body: Lower the free-shipping threshold and remodel bottom stores. Low cost, fast payback.

quadrants.heading: Strategic bets
quadrants.body: Automated replenishment and a member data platform. High value, longer build.

quadrants.heading: Keep improving
quadrants.body: Promotion calendar and service scripts stay in the regular operating rhythm.

quadrants.heading: Park for now
quadrants.body: Cross-border range and new-city pilots. Value is unclear, so we keep watching.

process.title: Automated replenishment rolls out in four steps
process.lead: Pilot first, then scale; each step has an exit criterion.

steps.heading: Prepare data
steps.body: Connect sales, stock and weather feeds

steps.heading: Change process
steps.body: Managers approve proposals instead of ordering

steps.heading: Scale
steps.body: Cover all stores and add to scorecards

process.conclusion: Exit criterion: 85% forecast accuracy and 1.5 pt lower spoilage.
